parsed.doc_summary: Morgan Lewis LawFlash (Aug 21, 2026) on algorithmic rent-pricing litigation. For in-scope jurisdictions, it describes Jersey City Code § 218-12 (June 2025), Hoboken City Code ch. 158 (July 2025), SF § 37.10C, San Diego §§ 98.1101-98.1104, Berkeley ch. 13.63 (Jan 2026 per this alert) and Santa Ana NS-3090 (April 2, 2026).

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ordinance is enforced publicly and privately, with fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.effective_date_note: Alert states 'effective June 2025'; day not given.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic rent coordination services; fines up to $2,000/day
rules.conflict_note: NJ FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43, eff. 7/1/2027) may preempt this ordinance once in effect; not described in this document.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.citation: Hoboken City Code ch. 158, Art. II
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.effective_date_note: Alert states 'effective July 2025'; day not given.
rules.key_value: ban on software/algorithms/data-sharing platforms to coordinate rents, lease terms, occupancy
rules.conflict_note: NJ FAIR Act may preempt once in effect; not described in this document.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance prohibits landlords from using qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month per unit may be a separate violation

rules.title: San Diego ban on algorithmic rent-setting
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use prohibited algorithmic rent-setting tools. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and penalties up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.quoted_span: San Diego similarly authorizes tenant suits for damages, injunctive relief and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and affected rental property potentially constituting a separate violation.
rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 per violation; each month and property may be separate

rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use coordinated rent-pricing algorithms. Violations can recur per unit per month and are privately enforceable.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms; recurring unit/month violations and private remedies
rules.effective_date_note: This alert says January 2026; the ordinance text reportedly says March 1, 2026 (not in this document).
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates: January 2026 (this alert) vs March 1, 2026 (ordinance text). Prefer the ordinance text.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing tools. Tenants may sue for up to $1,000 per violation per month.
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.key_value: up to $1,000 per violation per month
rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 per violation and per month
